description:
0000-CARDFILE-OPEN reports '10', and that is still a failure. THE TRAP THIS CASE EXISTS FOR: '10' is the benign end-of-file status everywhere else in this program, so an implementation that shared one status-handling routine between the OPEN and the READ would report a clean, empty, successful run here - two banners and RETURN-CODE 0 - where the source abends. The two paragraphs are deliberately different shapes. 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT is three-armed: app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:94 tests '00', :98 tests '10' explicitly, :99 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT and the 88-level APPL-EOF at :107 reads that as an orderly end, moving 'Y' into END-OF-FILE at :108. 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN is two-armed and does not test '10' at all: :121 asks only whether CARDFILE-STATUS = '00', so '10' falls to :124 MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT, and because the open paragraph carries no APPL-EOF arm the guard at :126 takes its ELSE. One file status, two call sites, benign at one and fatal at the other - which is precisely what gate G47 asks a case set to demonstrate rather than assume. WHAT THE CLASS NAME GETS WRONG: the unit under test is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob - an Account-named class in the account package - yet CBACT02C computes no balance and never touches the account file. It reads the CARD file. app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:29-33 is SELECT CARDFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO CARDFILE, ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY IS FD-CARD-NUM; :37-40 is an FD of FD-CARD-NUM X(16) plus FD-CARD-DATA X(134) = 150; and :45 is COPY CVACT02Y. AAP rule R1 governs - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and the divergence is catalogued in the register at AAP 0.8.4. A reviewer who trusts the class name will look for the wrong file and the wrong arithmetic. THE RUN, in source order: :71 displays the 38-character start banner; :72 performs 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN; the OPEN INPUT at :120 reports '10'; :121 takes its ELSE at :124; :126 takes its ELSE at :128; and the four-statement error arm runs - :129 DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE', :130 MOVE CARDFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS, :131 PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and :132 PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, which at :155-158 displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM', moves 0 to TIMING and 999 to ABCODE, and CALLs 'CEE3ABD'. RETURN-CODE is the 12 that :124 put in APPL-RESULT. THE STATUS IMAGE IS THE NUMERIC ARM: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS tests IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9' at :162-163, and '10' is numeric with a first byte that is not '9', so the ELSE at :170-172 runs - MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), overlaying positions three and four - giving the image '0010' and the line 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0010'. The trailing NNNN really is part of the COBOL literal at :172 and is not a placeholder awaiting substitution. case07 is this same numeric arm over '23', giving '0023'; case09 and case10 are the other half of the paragraph, the '9'-prefixed permanent-error convention that renders '9000'. Between them the four cases cover both arms of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS and, with the clean cases, both sides of '10'. NOTHING IS READ, AND THE LOOP IS NEVER ENTERED: :72 abends before :74, so the PERFORM UNTIL at :74-81, the DISPLAY CARD-RECORD at :78 and 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE at :83 are all unreached, no 150-byte record image appears among the expected lines, and the 36-character end banner at :85 is absent because :87 is never reached either. The browse handle acquired by the open is released on the way out silently and by contract - it emits no DISPLAY, issues no I/O and swallows any cleanup failure so the abend already unwinding is the one the caller sees - so it cannot add a line here, and it is not 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE: no close is issued, no close status is read, and 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE' is not this case's business. MESSAGE ARITHMETIC: 1 start banner + 0 record images + 3 diagnostic lines = 4 ordered DISPLAY_LINE entries, of widths 38, 22, 24 and 16. REPOSITORY STATUS SEQUENCE (gate G47): openBrowse reports '10' and the run abends; there is no readNext and no close, because :132 precedes both. The clean cases in this folder exercise the other side of the same value - readNext '10' as the orderly end of file - and case15 and case16 exercise the failing close this case cannot reach. The job is driven at tasklet/step level, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). THE WHOLE CARD MASTER IS SEEDED AND NOT ONE ROW OF IT IS READ: all 50 rows of carddata.txt are present, ascending on the RECORD KEY, each exactly the 150 bytes app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy declares - CARD-NUM PIC X(16) at 1-16, which is also the RECORD KEY; CARD-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) at 17-27; CARD-CVV-CD PIC 9(03) at 28-30; CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50) at 31-80; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10) at 81-90; CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) at 91; FILLER PIC X(59) at 92-150 - and 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150, so every seeded row ends in 59 significant spaces that must not be trimmed (gates G19 and G21). THE MISSPELLING IS THE CONTRACT: the copybook spells the date field CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE, missing the second T, exactly as CVACT01Y spells its own ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE; it is written verbatim wherever the field is named and is never silently corrected to CARD-EXPIRATION-DATE, because field-for-field diffing keys on the name (AAP implicit requirement I1). CVACT02Y declares no COMP-3, no PACKED-DECIMAL and no S9 anywhere, so both numeric spans - CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) and CARD-CVV-CD 9(03) - are unsigned zoned DISPLAY and no byte of this record is a sign overpunch. Seeding the complete, well-formed master is the point: a dataset can exist, hold every one of its records and be perfectly well formed, and still refuse to open. NOTHING IS WRITTEN: expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty, and that emptiness is a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest - :120 opens INPUT, the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE at all, and this run abends before it could reach one. No normalisation is declared, because carddata.txt rows are already the full 150 bytes CVACT02Y declares and neither recorded fixture-to-copybook deviation touches this file. WIRING: app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare //STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C with no PARM, and CBACT02C has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into, so jobParameters is empty; its single //CARDFILE DD at :25-26 is the only dataset, addressed here solely by the CARDFILE binding key that application.yml resolves at record length 150, so no dataset-name literal appears anywhere in this file (gate G46). ENCODING is US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default. PROVENANCE: every expected value in this file is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for each offset and width, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and DD contract, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the seeded rows. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution. AAP 0.7.6 proves such a run impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot be made executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator alongside three absent IBM copybooks, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler installable - and the substitution of provenance alone is recorded as risk R-A. Only the provenance changes; the 20 cases, the field-for-field diff and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand. GATES PINNED HERE: G15 (one of the twenty cases for this program), G18 (its diff count must be zero), G19 and G21 (the 150-byte seeded width and its space-filled FILLER), G35 (the CALL 'CEE3ABD' site raises an abend carrying RETURN-CODE 12, ABCODE 999 and TIMING 0, exactly as :154-158 sets them), G46 (binding key, never a DSNAME), G47 (this status at this call site) and G51 (asserted below the HTTP and JobLauncher layers). Not applicable: G30 and G32, since CBACT02C contains no GO TO; G33, since it declares no OCCURS; G16 and both right-pad normalisations, since carddata.txt needs neither; and G20 and G24 through G28, G37 through G43, since this program writes no record, performs no arithmetic beyond its own status bookkeeping and drives no screen. Fifty rows in, four lines out, RETURN-CODE 12.

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges an OPEN that reports DFHRESP(ENDFILE), which :121 treats as a failure like any other non-'00' outcome: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names OPEN-CARDFILE and gives it RESP 20. It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the shape used to be chosen by a switch over 'case01'..'case20' in CBACT02CParityTest, so this file showed the abend lines and said nothing about the condition that produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site reads its whole input and closes cleanly, so silence here is itself a statement. The outcome is a CICS RESP rather than a FILE STATUS because CardRepository reports this program's card-file outcomes as responses and AccountBalanceReaderJob translates them - declaring a status directly would skip the translation the case exists to judge.
